title: A Heuristic Framework of Variable Neighborhood Descent Methods for the Large-Scale Multi-Level Facility Location Problem in Supply Chain Networks
affiliations: Texas A&M International University and University of Mississippi

detail.title: A Heuristic Framework of Variable Neighborhood Descent Methods for the Large-Scale Multi-Level Facility Location Problem in Supply Chain Networks
detail.abstract: This paper addresses the single-assignment, uncapacitated, multi-level facility location (MFL) problem, a strategic decision-making process critical to the design of long-term supply chain networks. Specifically, we examine four-and five-level facility location structures (k-LFL), modeled as a location-allocation problem where demand nodes must be assigned to open facilities across hierarchical levels. Although the MFL has been addressed in the literature, solutions to large-scale, realistic problems involving thousands of nodes are lacking. This paper proposes a heuristic framework based on the Variable Neighborhood Descent (VND) metaheuristic with a multi-start strategy. We develop and compare four variants: Basic Variable Neighborhood Descent (BVND), Pipe Variable Neighborhood Descent (PVND), Cyclic Variable Neighborhood Descent (CVND), and Union Variable Neighborhood Descent (UVND). In each case, a multi-start strategy with strong diversification components is employed. Extensive computational experiments compare the methods on large-scale instances involving up to 10,000 customers, 150 distribution centers, 50 warehouses, and 30 plants. Each algorithm settled into a unique, statistically significant computational time when solving these problems. Sensitivity analyses, supported by nonparametric statistical methods, validate the effectiveness of the proposed heuristic framework.

detail.title: How and why do users in Non-Western Countries use AI Chatbots? A Systematic Literature Review

publicationDetails.detailsText: This paper was submitted to Telematics and Informatics Reports on 17 February 2026

detail.abstract: Existing research on AI chatbots predominantly focuses on Western contexts. To address this gap, we conducted a systematic literature review (2019-2024) examining the development, use, and acceptance of AI chatbots by users in business organisations in non-Western countries. We investigate the influence of culture on individual-level technology acceptance. We utilise the revised Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (revised UTAUT) developed in 2022 as our theoretical framework to explain our findings. By presenting the cross-cultural differences, this framework highlights how the impact of AI chatbots may vary between non-Western countries and the Western world. Our synthesis of the literature highlights the significance of the revised UTAUT predictors, the functions and features of AI chatbots, and the languages used that affect the use of the technology. We identify key drivers and critical barriers to the use of AI chatbots, notably government restrictions and a lack of training datasets in non-Western languages. Hence, we offer a comprehensive understanding of AI chatbots' acceptance within diverse non-Western countries.

title: GWDGN: A Novel Gaussian Weighted Domain Generalization Network for Thermal Power Unit Short-Term Load Forecasting
affiliations: Shanghai University of Electric Power, Shanghai University of Electric Power, Shanghai University of Electric Power and  Huaneng Songyuan Thermal Power Plant

detail.title: GWDGN: A Novel Gaussian Weighted Domain Generalization Network for Thermal Power Unit Short-Term Load Forecasting
detail.abstract: Data-driven approaches have shown remarkable efficacy in the short-term load forecasting of thermal power units. However, existing approaches typically rely on the assumption that data follows an identical distribution. In reality, distribution shifts occur both across different generating units and throughout the temporal operation phases of individual units. To mitigate this challenge, this study proposes a Gaussian weighted domain generalization network (GWDGN). The methodology comprises two key components, temporal domain segmentation and distribution alignment. Initially, a Gaussian mixture model automatically segments the operational data into multiple temporal subdomains with distinctive distribution characteristics. Subsequently, the domain adversarial strategy realizes the distributional alignment, while a weighted smoothing label strategy is designed in the adversarial training process to improve the stability of adversarial training. Comprehensive experiments utilizing actual operational data from four thermal power units demonstrate that GWDGN significantly outperforms conventional domain generalization methods, achieving performance improvements of 29.1% to 50.3% across cross unit transfer scenarios. Moreover, t-SNE visualization analysis further confirms that after GWDGN processing, the feature distributions across different units achieved significant alignment.

detail.abstract: The emergence of autonomous AI agents as active participants in B2B commerce requires a fundamental revision of how enterprises conceptualize digital visibility. Existing disciplines-Search Engine Optimization (SEO), Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), and Generative Engine Optimization (GEO)-address visibility in contexts where a human user ultimately drives the decision process. This paper argues that a new category of visibility challenges arises when autonomous agents, acting on behalf of organizations, evaluate and select suppliers, initiate negotiations, and execute transactions without direct human involvement at the moment of decision. We introduce the AI Visibility Stack, a three-layer conceptual framework that maps the complete spectrum of enterprise visibility in AI-mediated environments: (1) LLM Visibility, addressed by AEO and GEO; (2) Agent Discoverability, addressed by the newly proposed discipline of Agent Discovery Optimization (ADO); and (3) Agent Participation, addressed by Agent Presence Optimization (APO). We describe the technical infrastructure underpinning this ecosystem-principally Google's Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol and Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP)-and propose the ADO Score as a composite metric for measuring agentic discoverability. The framework is contextualized against projected market data indicating that AI agents will intermediate over $15 trillion in B2B spending globally by 2028. Implications for enterprise digital strategy, particularly for B2B companies in Spanish-speaking markets, are discussed.

title: Accounting vs. Sustainability Reports in Mining Waste Management: Transparency with Corruption in Latin America
affiliations: Universidad Nacional de Córdoba, Universidad Nacional del Litoral and York University - Atkinson School of Administrative Studies

detail.title: Accounting vs. Sustainability Reports in Mining Waste Management: Transparency with Corruption in Latin America

declarations.funderStatement: This work was supported by a PSI grant from Chartered Professional Accountants of Ontario and a York University Research Support Grant.

detail.abstract: We study the role of accounting and sustainability disclosures in the transparency of mining waste management when there are negative social and environmental outcomes. We report on a longitudinal descriptive case built on two events from Brazil using mandated sustainability and accounting reports. The appearance of transparency, facilitated by corrupt practices and actors, and its links with environmental and social disasters, is explored through performativity theory. Saying something can produce a real outcome that changes reality; therefore, this study counts specific words and how they are used in sustainability and financial reports before and after each event. We ask if accounting reports resulting from professional practices and artifacts deter corruption in publicly traded companies as much as mandated environmental and social reports. Corruption is understood as the devastation of the poor and we explore the disclosures given to stakeholders as a form of transparency. We conclude that neither the apparent transparency nor the complete silence was able to avoid social catastrophes in Brazil affecting poor rural areas; however, accounting reports give the appearance of more transparency than sustainability reports. However, accounting practices and artifacts provide more disclosures increasing the visibility of suspected corruption, with the difference explained by the extensive accounting regulation that restricts management exclusionary practices for their reports. A description of transparency through the role of accounting and sustainability disclosures enhances our understanding of fertile grounds for corrupt practices in Latin America. The way transparency is enacted, predisposes government officers, managers and auditors to engage in corrupt practices.

detail.abstract: This professional case study evaluates the design and implementation of a standardized HR system in a small faith-based nonprofit organization, "Church A." Using qualitative document analysis, this study examines governance structures, a Paid Time Off (PTO) policy, job analysis instruments, job descriptions, performance review procedures, and a 360-degree pastoral evaluation tool. Findings indicate strong governance clarity and well-defined policies, with detailed job analysis contributing to improved role clarity. Weaknesses include lack of behavioral anchors in evaluations, inconsistent alignment between job documentation and appraisal criteria, and limited developmental guidance associated with multisource feedback. Recommendations include job-specific performance addenda, behavioral anchors, rater calibration, and structured post-360 development plans. This case demonstrates how small nonprofits can build coherent, evidence-based HR systems aligned with I/O psychology principles despite limited resources.

title: Purpose-Built Payment Infrastructure for Autonomous AI Agents
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Purpose-Built Payment Infrastructure for Autonomous AI Agents

keywords: digital payments Agent-Based Simulation V.C. Study 2: Controlled Experiment V.D. Study 3: Technology Adoption Survey V.E. Comparative Protocol Analysis V.F. Limitations and Mitigation

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence agents are emerging as autonomous economic actors capable of initiating, negotiating, and settling financial transactions without human intervention, yet the payment infrastructure they require does not exist in adequate form. Legacy payment rails (card networks, ACH, wire transfers) impose minimum transaction thresholds, human-centric authentication requirements, and batch settlement cycles that are structurally incompatible with agent transaction patterns characterized by sub-cent micropayments, millisecond settlement demands, and programmatic API access. This paper argues that purpose-built infrastructure bridging stablecoin programmability with fiat universality, governed by graduated autonomy frameworks, represents the structurally optimal architectural response. Employing a mixed-methods approach that combines transaction cost analysis, agent-based simulation design, comparative protocol evaluation across six production systems (x402, AP2, ACP, Visa TAP, Mastercard Agent Pay, Skyfire KYAPay), and regulatory framework analysis, the paper advances five principal findings. First, stablecoin Layer 2 rails enable a 100-to-1,000-fold cost reduction for agent-typical transactions relative to card network settlement. Second, aggregation strategies optimized for agent workload characteristics achieve greater than ninety percent settlement cost reduction compared to per-transaction processing. Third, multi-homing dynamics specific to AI agents prevent the winner-take-all protocol tipping predicted by classical network effects theory. Fourth, graduated autonomy outperforms both fully autonomous and fully supervised authorization regimes on task completion, error cost, and time-to-completion metrics. Fifth, privacy-preserving compliance constitutes a prerequisite, not merely an enhancement, for regulated-sector adoption.

detail.abstract: We challenge the prevailing assumption of generative AI integration in commercial design: that AI-generated visual communication yields equivalent consumer emotional response and behavioral intent as human-authored content. We evaluate consumer aesthetic response within an empirical framework that preserves cross-cultural dependencies across Indian, Middle Eastern, and multicultural Western markets. Leveraging a longitudinal practitioner dataset of commercial A/B testing and live audience evaluation, we observe a persistent "AI penalty"-a significant deterioration in perceived credibility and emotional resonance when visual assets are attributed to generative algorithms. Diverse cultural contexts maintain a statistically robust credibility gap, albeit with varying severity influenced by regional aesthetic frameworks (e.g., Rasa theory). The observed aesthetic deficit dominates the cost-efficiency gains of AI generation, undermining brand trust and purchase intention. Commercial practitioners need highly localized, human-in-the-loop interventions to match the emotional utility of traditional design. Our findings indicate that brands relying solely on zero-shot AI generation require substantially higher media spend to achieve the expected consumer engagement utility of human-created campaigns.

detail.title: Market Return Decomposition and Equity Risk Premium Predictability
detail.abstract: We introduce a novel decomposition of stock market returns into a fundamental component (FC), capturing long-term growth, and an unexpected capital gain component (UC), reflecting short-term fluctuations. The decomposition is explicit, straightforward to estimate, and designed to correct model misspecification in traditional predictive regressions. The FC aligns with highly persistent valuation ratios, while the UC is predictable via standard regressions, further improved by shrinkage. Using 41 predictors from Goyal et al. (2024), we find 33 significant predictors of market returns, compared with only 5 in their study. Combining forecasts across predictors reaffirm equity risk premium predictability out-of-sample.

title: Adverse Selection in the AI Data Commons
affiliations: Bocconi University

detail.title: Adverse Selection in the AI Data Commons
detail.abstract: Generative AI depends on high-quality web content, yet no market compensates its producers. We document adverse selection in this AI data commons: facing a binary opt-out choice, the highest-quality producers exit first, degrading the remaining commons. Studying media and news sites at scale, we find a steep quality-blocking gradient: high-factual outlets block at nearly six times the rate of low-factual sources, with misinformation sources remaining most accessible. Publishers strategically target training crawlers while blocking search crawlers at lower rates. Event studies trace this divergence to the introduction of AI-specific opt-out mechanisms, and simulations show the quality degradation stems from the compositional pattern of exit. Current opt-out regimes produce adverse selection by design; our findings call for market mechanisms that properly compensate content producers.

title: Financial Benefits and Consequences of Organizational Citizenship Behavior in the Banking Industry

detail.title: Financial Benefits and Consequences of Organizational Citizenship Behavior in the Banking Industry
detail.abstract: Organizational citizenship behavior (OCB) has emerged as a strategically significant yet operationally complex phenomenon within the banking industry, where discretionary employee behavior directly influences service quality, performance outcomes, and financial positioning. This literature review examines the dual nature of OCB through a balanced analysis of its organizational benefits and consequences, with particular attention to the financial implications of both its cultivation and overreliance. Drawing on empirical and theoretical research spanning banking, financial services, and adjacent high-compliance industries, this review synthesizes findings across four thematic dimensions: the conceptual foundations of OCB in banking, the performance and financial benefits of sustained OCB, the employee-level consequences of excessive OCB including emotional exhaustion and citizenship fatigue, and the organizational risk factors that undermine discretionary behavior. Findings indicate that while OCB demonstrably enhances performance proxies such as efficiency, service quality, and customer satisfaction, its benefits follow a non-linear trajectory that is highly contingent on organizational climate, managerial behavior, and structural resource design. The review concludes that sustainable OCB in banking requires intentional cultivation through supportive internal systems, psychological ownership conditions, and guardrails against implicit performance expectation, rather than assumptive reliance on employee goodwill. Implications for banking leadership and future research directions are discussed.

title: Valuing the Modern Athlete: A New Framework for the Billion-Dollar Nil Market

detail.title: Valuing the Modern Athlete: A New Framework for the Billion-Dollar Nil Market
detail.abstract: The collegiate athletic landscape has transitioned into a hyper-liquid capital market estimated at $1.2 billion annually, currently characterized by information asymmetry and high-velocity athlete mobility. This paper identifies a fundamental valuation crisis termed the "53% Problem," where non-athletic cultural variables explain over half of the variance in valuations while athletic performance accounts for only 18%. This disconnect leads to Efficiency Regression, a documented decline in performance metrics for high-earning transfers whose compensation is not grounded in athletic utility. To introduce stability into this chaotic environment, we propose a framework rooted in Control Theory from systems engineering, conceptualizing the NIL ecosystem as a dynamic system requiring an algorithmic "feedback loop" to stabilize institutional capital. The methodology employs a Four-Core Valuation Model-synthesizing performance (45%), market (25%), brand (20%), and risk (10%)-to establish a defensible Fair Market Value (FMV) and calculate the Cost-Per-Win-Share (CPWS). Central to our risk assessment is the "Mercenary Score," a proprietary metric utilizing psycholinguistic profiling to distinguish between transactional "mercenaries" and institutionally aligned "missionaries". By adopting these standards, universities and collectives secure "Fiduciary Insurance," providing the "rebuttable presumption of reasonableness" necessary for IRS §4958 compliance and College Sports Commission (CSC) oversight. Ultimately, this framework enables a transition from speculative gambling to strategic roster investing, ensuring that capital deployment aligns with verifiable on-field utility.

Evidence from a Large E-Commerce Platform

detail.title:
Entry and Advertising on Digital Platforms 
Evidence from a Large E-Commerce Platform
detail.abstract: Millions of businesses join digital platforms each year, yet little is known about their success rates or how platforms manage their entry. Using data from a leading Chinese e-commerce platform, we show that fewer than 1% of new, ID-verified sellers become successful small-to-medium-sized businesses. Analysis of search sessions reveals that consumers prefer entrant products over incumbent ones. Further, increasing entrant exposure on the margin increases overall purchase rate of a search session, indicating that entrants are under-explored compared to the social optimum. Finally, we revisit a prior intervention on the platform that increased entrant advertising. We find that it promoted entry with minimal impact on screening efficiency. A model of platform-mediated entry explains our findings and predicts how platform maturity, entrant quality, and advertising jointly determine optimal exploration.

detail.abstract: The dominant paradigm for integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into Security Operations Centers (SOCs), which this paper terms prescribed intelligence (human-engineered skills, hardcoded tool integrations, and prompt templates), is structurally insufficient for replicating the adaptive workflows of expert SOC analysts. This paper identifies five limitations of that paradigm and proposes credentialed self-exploration as an alternative: provision an LLM agent with strictly read-only access to a sandboxed or test SOC environment, describe its role, and let it autonomously discover data sources, learn tool relationships, and propose executable skills for human review. During exploration, the agent takes no action on production systems; only skills that pass human review are deployed. The paper introduces AESOP (Agent-driven Exploration for Security Operations Proficiency), a conceptual framework for this self-directed architecture, and outlines a research agenda for empirical validation. Supporting evidence draws on cross-domain advances in tool learning, autonomous agents, and offensive security (penetration testing), demonstrating patterns transferable to defensive SOC operations-a central question this work raises.

title: Critical Minerals: Global Palladium Supply & Demand

detail.title: Critical Minerals: Global Palladium Supply & Demand
detail.abstract: As the world moves toward greener technologies, the demand for strategic commodities is on the rise. One such commodity, palladium, is crucial for automotive catalysts, electronics, and hydrogen fuel cells. With the majority of the world's palladium supply concentrated in South Africa and Russia, geopolitical tensions and supply constraints could significantly impact this essential metal. As a result, policymakers and industries worldwide must be prepared to address the challenges associated with securing reliable and sustainable palladium supply chains. Palladium is a precious metal belonging to the platinum-group metals (PGMs), which includes platinum, rhodium, iridium, osmium, and ruthenium. Palladium is most often extracted as a byproduct of mining for platinum and nickel. Thus, market demand and prices for platinum and/or nickel figure significantly in the economics of palladium production. Characterized by its silvery-white appearance, palladium is valued for its resistance to corrosion, excellent catalytic properties, and ability to absorb hydrogen. Its unique combination of properties makes palladium a sought-after material for various applications, particularly in the automotive and electronics industries.

detail.abstract: International humanitarian law (IHL) has been under immense pressure in the past few years. Despite IHL being created to mitigate suffering in armed conflicts, in recent years it has been leveraged by some as a means of justifying violence against civilians under the guise of proportionate incidental loss. With IHL lacking organic international accountability mechanisms, some States have “gamed” the rules of this body of law, resulting in military operations causing the deaths of tens of thousands of civilians that are defended as legally justifiable. Such arguments are a far cry from the original founding impetus of IHL, based on Dunant’s idea of humanity as “a kind of energy which gives one a positive craving to relieve as many as one can”. In this article, we argue that to re-emphasize humanity, it might be necessary to focus on other means of accounting for civilian harm, whether it is lawful or unlawful. Traditionally, criminal prosecutions have punished grave breaches of IHL or war crimes, neglecting the place of redress. Other bodies of international law, such as international human rights law, have expanded litigation possibilities for individual civilian harm in armed conflict at both the domestic and international level. Many of these cases have helped shape the key components of human rights law and have provided a strong incentive for States to ensure rights, protect victims and prevent future violations. Yet lawful civilian harm, where States find that incidental civilian loss is not excessive in relation to the military advantage gained, may provide no legal avenue to a claim of a violation of IHL or human rights law.

title: Essequibo: Guyana-Venezuela Territorial Dispute with Energy Implications

detail.title: Essequibo: Guyana-Venezuela Territorial Dispute with Energy Implications
detail.abstract: The International Court of Justice (ICJ) delivered a ruling on Thursday affirming that the court has jurisdiction over a long-standing territorial dispute between Venezuela and Guyana. The dispute involves the contested territory of Essequibo, which encompasses nearly two-thirds of Guyana's sovereign territory. The ruling is in response to an objection made by Venezuela, which has reiterated that the ICJ has no jurisdiction over the territorial dispute, and has instead pushed for bilateral talks with Guyana to resolve the situation. The territorial dispute over the Essequibo has been ongoing for over a century, dating back to Guyana's colonial period. In 1899, an arbitration tribunal awarded the Essequibo to Great Britain, which ruled Guyana at the time. Venezuela rejected the decision, and the dispute has continued to this day, with occasional flareups in tensions between Caracas and Georgetown over the subject. In its legal proceedings with the ICJ, Guyana's argument insists that the 1899 arbitration served as the effective conclusion of the dispute, thereby affirming Guyana's current sovereignty over the entire territory.

title: Lithium OPEC: Viable or Volatile?

detail.title: Lithium OPEC: Viable or Volatile?
detail.abstract: In an effort to collectively boost their bargaining power, Argentina, Chile, and Bolivia, and Brazil are exploring the idea of forming an OPEC-like cartel for the lithium industry. The four states hold nearly 65% of the world's lithium reserves, and the proposed group would mirror OPEC's functions of coordinating production and pricing, while standardizing practices in a nascent and strategic market for the region. However, bringing the idea to fruition is likely to spark opposition from the industry, as well as internal political opposition from environmentalists and indigenous groups that contributed to left-wing victories in Chile, Argentina, and Brazil. Furthermore, additional obstacles include China's monopolist position in the industry and the long-term political viability of such an idea.

title: Central Bank Gold Rush: Temporary Haven or Permanent Pivot?

detail.title: Central Bank Gold Rush: Temporary Haven or Permanent Pivot?
detail.abstract: In defiance of industry predictions, demand for gold in 2023 has persisted, due in large part to the bulk purchases made by central banks worldwide. Data from the World Gold Council indicates that central banks have bolstered their gold reserves significantly, with WGC analyst Krishan Gopaul adding that year-to-date purchases in 2023 exemplify "the strongest start to a year back to at least 2010-when central banks became net buyers on an annual basis." Furthermore, gold prices have rebounded significantly since November 2022, with current prices hovering around $2,000/oz, not far from the record high price notched back in August 2020. Underlying this demand for gold is a confluence of domestic and geopolitical factors. This article will examine the key motives that have influenced central banks' decision-making, aiming to shed light on the persistence in gold's appeal to central banks. Gold, traditionally seen as a safe-haven asset, provides central banks with a reliable store of value in times of economic uncertainty. The latest surge in gold purchases can be attributed to growing concerns over rising inflation, currency devaluation, and the desire to diversify central bank holdings. Actions undertaken by the US Federal Reserve have been particularly influential, with US rate hikes and a resilient dollar compelling several central banks to turn to gold as a hedge in preserving the value of their reserves. Gold prices rallied further amid the collapse of Silicon Valley Bank, a US-based bank, sparking concerns of a cascading banking crisis and contagion. Though some forecasts suggest the banking crisis could prompt a Fed "pivot" in interest.

detail.abstract: This article introduces the Enduring Impact Architecture™ (EIA Framework), a model for building mission-driven organizations capable of sustaining purpose and operational capacity across decades of inevitable turbulence. There is a critical distinction between generating impact and sustaining it. Early achievements-policy wins, programmatic growth, market traction-do not guarantee institutional longevity. Growth does not equal durability. Scale does not eliminate fragility. An organization that produces significant impact for five years but collapses during a funding contraction has generated influence, not durability. An institution that survives multiple political cycles, economic downturns, leadership transitions, and cultural shifts without abandoning its core mission demonstrates endurance. Endurance requires intentional architecture and the EIA Framework provides a starting point on how to design organizations that assume disruptions will occur and are intent on being prepared to overcome them.

detail.title: Framework of theoretical Research and Prospects on Postdoctoral Training
detail.abstract: This framework presents the theoretical research of postdoctoral training, aiming to explore the postdoctoral stage as a key link in cultivating independent scientific research talents. The document constructs four core frameworks, including socialization theory, human capital theory, ecosystem model and career theory, and deeply analyzes the process of postdoctoral transformation from "dependent" to "independent", emphasizing the importance of human capital investment and the supporting role of multi-level ecosystems in growth. The core consensus in this paper points out that the training goal should shift from a single scientific research output to cultivating independent innovators, the role of mentors should be transformed into career development partners, and the training content should take into account both professional and transferable skills. In addition, the document also looks forward to future research challenges such as globalization, mental health, AI technology, and non-academic paths, and advocates translating theory into specific policies and practices to support the development of diverse postdoctoral careers through institutional environment optimization and data-driven evaluation.

detail.abstract: This thesis examines what threats the data broker industry and surveillance capitalism pose to individuals, organizations, and homeland security. Through a qualitative analysis of open-source material grounded in social contract theory, it argues that the commercial collection, aggregation, and sale of personal data produce an inescapable digital panopticon. This system enables harms ranging from fraud and stalking to microtargeting of military, law enforcement, and government personnel by foreign adversaries. Current legal frameworks, including Fourth Amendment jurisprudence and notice-and-consent models, are inadequate, creating a coercive environment where privacy is eroded and meaningful consent is illusory. The research highlights a paradox: the data streams used by security agencies for legitimate purposes are exploited by adversaries to create vulnerabilities. This thesis concludes that entrenched, unregulated data infrastructure constitutes a persistent security threat ripe for weaponization. It contends that infrastructures enabling personalization and operational benefits also fuel coercion, discrimination, and physical threats. Thus, it recommends federal regulation establishing fiduciary duties for data collectors coupled with robust digital literacy education, immediate personal security mitigations for vulnerable practitioners, and the development of capabilities by the United States to leverage this data ecosystem offensively against foreign threats.

detail.abstract: This study examines the traditional agricultural and fishing systems that flourished in Biliran Province prior to industrialization. These practices, rooted in communal cooperation and ecological balance, sustained rural life through coconut and abaca farming, barter exchange, and artisanal fishing. Yet, such traditions remain under-documented, often dismissed as "ordinary" history. Employing oral history interviews, archival sources, and ethnographic fieldwork, the research reconstructs these pre-industrial livelihoods and situates them within cultural and environmental sustainability frameworks. Findings indicate that pre-industrial methods promoted social cohesion, economic equity, and ecological balance values increasingly lost under industrialized modes of production. The study highlights the importance of preserving traditional knowledge as intangible heritage and as a foundation for sustainable rural development in the 21st century.

detail.title: A Geometric and Probabilistic Framework for Equity Market Microstructure Rigorous Core with Rough-path Dynamics and Conditional Thermodynamic Extensions
detail.abstract:
We develop a mathematical framework for equity market microstructure that separates proved model-class results from explicitly assumption-driven extensions. The rigorous core models the limit order book as a non-negative Radon measure with weak-form dynamics driven by compensated Poisson integration and an explicit cancellation kernel; defines a distributional bid-ask spread as a Wasserstein-2 distance between midprice-centred liquidity profiles under finite-second-moment assumptions; derives the corresponding Benamou-Brenier liquidity-cost representation; proves a benchmark ex ante root-mean-square spread lower bound from a sequential trade model, a competitive adverse-selection bridge, and the van Trees inequality; obtains an exact KL decomposition of informational displacement into permanent and transient components; and establishes existence of a fixed-point equilibrium in a reduced mean field game with discrete dealer inventories under a single explicit feedback-continuity hypothesis. 

A further scaling extension treats long-memory signed order flow through a Marcus/Volterra rough-path perspective and identifies the critical propagator exponent β c = 2H-1 under explicit scaling, kernel, self-consistency, and Volterra-admissibility assumptions. The information-theoretic layer proves non-negative path-space KL entropy production for observable market states. Stronger statistical-mechanical claims-a Crooks-type fluctuation theorem, a cost-variance relation, and a liquid/illiquid instability criterion-are formulated only under additional stochastic-thermodynamic closure assumptions and are offered as falsifiable hypotheses rather than unconditional laws. The paper is therefore intended as a theory framework: Sections 2-4 contain the cleanest rigorous core, Section 5 adds a scaling theorem under an explicit Volterra-admissibility hypothesis, and Section 6 separates rigorous informationtheoretic statements from conditional thermodynamic consequences. Calibration and falsification are deferred to future empirical work.

detail.title: Public Policy Analysis of the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 and Punjab Juvenile Justice Rules: A Case Study of Punjab, India
detail.abstract: This study aims to assess the implementation of the juvenile justice system as a public policy intervention in the context of the state of Punjab, with special reference to the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, and the Punjab Juvenile Justice Rules. The juvenile justice system is based on the concept of reformative justice and the welfare of the child and aims to provide justice to children in conflict with the law as well as to those in need of care and protection. The paper attempts to discuss the context of the juvenile justice system from the larger perspective of the socio-economic scenario and the factors such as poverty, substance abuse, migration, and educational deprivations that affect the juveniles in the state of Punjab. It also attempts to discuss the development of the legal framework and the institutional mechanisms with reference to the state of Punjab. Finally, the study concludes with the recommendations that could be made to the existing system of juvenile justice with reference to the state of Punjab.

title:
The Verification Paradox 
How Checking Makes Commitment Networks Look Worse and Work Better
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title:
The Verification Paradox 
How Checking Makes Commitment Networks Look Worse and Work Better
detail.abstract: Whether someone checks a commitment matters more than what the commitment contains. We analyze 69,847 condition-review observations across 56,515 unique IMF lending conditions in 1,798 programs and find that the dynamics of institutional commitments split into two regimes at a sharp boundary: the moment of verification. Before the promisee checks, conditions stagnate with decreasing hazard rates (Weibull k = 0.37)-73% of conditions are never assessed, and those that survive past the second review become exponentially harder to resolve. After the promisee checks, dynamics become physics-like with near-constant hazard (k = 0.90)-outcomes are honest, predictable, and independent of dwell time. An XGBoost classifier (AUC 0.93) confirms the pattern: it predicts assessment transitions accurately but collapses to near-random for post-assessment outcomes, exactly where constant-hazard dynamics make features irrelevant. This produces a paradox: programs that verify aggressively score worse on health metrics because verification surfaces failures that would otherwise remain invisible. The shape parameter k, measurable from any time series of commitment outcomes, serves as a diagnostic for institutional dynamics-it predicts where machine learning will succeed, quantifies the cost of delayed assessment, and varies systematically across 91 countries (0.17 to 0.87), review positions (halving by review 11), and historical periods (improving since 2016 as program sizes declined). Both regimes are real features of institutional life. The pathology is not stagnation itself but involuntary stagnationcommitments that compost by default because nobody checked, rather than by deliberate choice.

detail.abstract: This article examines how Nigeria's limited security resources are systematically diverted from public protection to serve private elite interests. Drawing on interviews with 27 security personnel across multiple agencies and extensive secondary sources, the study reveals that police resources, constitutionally mandated to serve all citizens equally, have become commodified services available primarily to those with financial means and political connections. The research employs three theoretical frameworks: wicked problems theory explains why decades of reform consistently fail; elite capture theory demonstrates how colonial institutional legacies enable systematic resource appropriation; and strain theory illuminates how poverty wages and institutional neglect drive individual officers into patron-client relationships with elites. With almost one-third of Nigeria's 370,000 police officers assigned to VIP protection rather than public service, this commodification erodes public safety, undermines democratic principles of equal citizenship, and perpetuates cycles of dysfunction resistant to conventional reform approaches.

detail.title: Digital Infrastructure and Export of SMEs: Evidence from China
detail.abstract: This paper shows that digital infrastructure development improves SMEs' performance on the international market in China. Using a staggered Difference-inDifferences (DID) design and data from SMEs listed on the A-share SME and ChiNext board (2009-2020), we find that the Broadband China policy significantly boosts SME exports. On average, SMEs located in the pilot cities enjoyed a 6.3% larger increase in export-to-revenue compared to those located elsewhere. Our results are robust to the use of new DID estimators, Goodman-Bacon (2021) decomposition, Propensity Score Matching (PSM), pre-trend analysis, placebo tests, and alternative samples. The impact of the policy varies with firm size, industry, and executive team composition. The Broadband China policy promotes digital transformation of SMEs, which facilitates export through enhanced direct market access, reduced transactional costs, and alleviated financial constraints. We also provide evidence that rules out improvements in productivity or imports as drivers of the observed export expansion.

title: Corporate Governance and Trade Credit: International Evidence from Board Reforms
affiliations: Stevens Institute of Technology - School of Business, Utah State University - Huntsman School of Business, Brock University - Department of Finance, Operations and Information Systems (FOIS) and University of California, Los Angeles (UCLA)

detail.title: Corporate Governance and Trade Credit: International Evidence from Board Reforms
detail.abstract: Drawing on current literature, this study develops a simple external financing model and provides international evidence of the causal effects of corporate governance improvements on trade credit. We introduce an internal governance perspective, hypothesizing that weak internal governance, which fosters managerial agency problems, allows firm managers to misuse trade credit. Specifically, poor governance may lead firms to rely on supplier financing as a substitute for traditional financing when they face financing constraints, a practice the literature argues raises concerns about shifting a firm's financial burdens onto its suppliers. Using a decade of data surrounding governance-enhancing board reforms in 38 countries, our difference-indifferences analyses strongly support these predictions. We find that strengthening board oversight via exogenous reforms reduces firms' reliance on supplier financing. Improved internal governance decreases firms' dependence on supplier financing and limits the manipulation of payables through real earnings management activities, such as inventory overproduction, which affects accounts payable. We also find that the effect of internal governance reforms is most pronounced in countries with stronger external governance mechanisms, suggesting a complementary effect. Additionally, our findings show that enhanced governance leads to better investment decisions and improved firm performance, especially for financially constrained firms and those with high agency costs.

detail.abstract:
Payment card markets are globally dominated by a few large card networks, which give significant rebates to issuing banks. Policy makers are concerned about rising merchant fees and the overreliance on these networks’ payment services. A common assumption is that profitable entry is blockaded by the entry costs to set up the payment system and network, resulting in a monopolistic or duopolistic market structure. The question analyzed in this paper is under which conditions a card network sets rebates at a higher level such that competitors cannot profitably enter the market. Deterrence becomes more profitable for a large card network when transaction benefits increase - especially if issuing banks pass rebates through to cardholders. At the same time, entry becomes more blockaded if issuing banks face costs to switch their card issuance
to a different card network - indicating that large card networks may use rebates to increase switching costs. These lock-in effects explain why domestic card networks are pushed aside and new card networks struggle to gain ground and may have important implications for payment regulation.

detail.abstract: The General Services Administration's proposed contract clause, GSAR 552.239-7001, attempts to embed AI governance into federal procurement through a single default instrument applied across GSA's commercial buying channels. The clause addresses real gaps in federal AI acquisition, including inadequate transparency, weak exit rights, insufficient testing authority, opaque supply chains, and unchecked vendor dependency. But it responds by aggregating buyer protections, operational control, sourcing mandates, and politically derived performance conditions into one overburdened clause. This essay examines what the draft gets right, where it overreaches, and why the federal government's rapid shift from an AI governance vacuum to a sweeping, politically charged contract clause is not the corrective the procurement system needs.

title: BLT Engine: Crisis-Alpha Validation Across Crypto Market Regimes

detail.title: BLT Engine: Crisis-Alpha Validation Across Crypto Market Regimes
detail.abstract: This paper validates the Boutgajouft Liquidity Triangle (BLT) systematic trading framework in cryptocurrency markets across three distinct regimes (2020-2022). Following 17 years of traditional market validation demonstrating Alpha = 0.00 and Beta = 0.00 across all periods, we extend the framework to digital assets. Results demonstrate consistent profitability: +220% CAGR during the 2020 COVID crash (vs. BTC -58%), +414% CAGR in the 2021 bull market (Sharpe 6.82, top 1% performance), and +15.8% CAGR in the 2022 bear market with Beta -0.158 (profit while BTC declined -64%). Average Sharpe ratio: 4.39. The strategy maintains top-quartile market-neutral positioning for cryptocurrency markets (Beta 0.29 average, range -0.16 to +0.63) while preserving crisis-alpha characteristics: positive correlation between volatility and returns. Transaction costs remain below 2% of profits with ultra-low turnover (10-25 trades/year). This represents the first documented case of a systematic strategy achieving both perfect neutrality in traditional markets and top-quartile performance in cryptocurrency markets within the same theoretical framework, validating cross-asset adaptability of liquidity triangle geometry.

detail.abstract: We study how federal information-collection requirements affect public infrastructure spending of local governments. Exploiting the introduction and revision of the federal survey on highway infrastructure, we find that county roads that are randomly sampled by the survey attract more local government spending. The increased spending is concentrated in capital outlays for road improvements and is somewhat pronounced for roads in poor condition. The spending seems successful in expanding the county road network and usage and reducing fatalities. Collectively, our evidence suggests that federal information-collection efforts shape the allocation of resources by providing information on road segments in need of resources but also by directing attention and resources to roads that happen to be sampled, irrespective of their need for resources.

detail.abstract: We show that investors treat individual stocks as weak substitutes, and that this weak substitutability explains the existence of the "factor zoo" in expected stock returns. In classical asset-pricing models, substitutability is strong: investors readily reallocate across assets that covary, so differences in expected returns are explained by the few factors that contribute most to covariances across stocks. In contrast, we show that substitutability is empirically weak by measuring cross-sectional return predictability, cross-price multipliers, and cross-price elasticities. This weak substitutability gives rise to the factor zoo: expected returns depend on many factors, including weak factors that drive little covariance across stocks. Moreover, weak substitutability rationalizes why equilibrium Sharpe ratios remain moderate even though weak factors contribute to expected returns. Additionally, weak substitutability implies that misspecified substitution patterns create only small biases in price elasticity and multiplier estimates.

detail.abstract: Transitioning from internal combustion vehicles (ICEs) to battery electric vehicles (BEVs) is essential for achieving many nations' climate goals. Although BEV adoption is rising, it varies substantially across regions and remains low in many countries despite significant investment from automakers and governments. Prior research has emphasized behavioral impediments to adoption, like range anxiety, and explored infrastructure design to support BEVs, often relying on surveys or niche settings like car sharing. However, little is known about how BEVs are used in everyday life, how their usage compares to ICEs, and how charging infrastructure shapes these patterns. Using telemetry data from 300,000 U.S. vehicles, we show that, contrary survey-based evidence, modern BEVs are driven as frequently and far as ICEs, with only modest differences in long-distance travel. Refueling behavior further challenges common assumptions about range anxiety. When away from home, BEV and ICE users are equally likely to refuel at a given remaining range. Near home, however, BEV users—including those without home chargers—refuel more often than ICE users even when the remaining range is high, underscoring the critical role of home-proximate charging access. These insights can inform BEV service design and charging infrastructure policy.

title: Impact of Referral Ties on Worker Earnings in the Gig Economy: Evidence from an On-Demand Delivery Platform in India

detail.title: Impact of Referral Ties on Worker Earnings in the Gig Economy: Evidence from an On-Demand Delivery Platform in India
detail.abstract: With digital platform "gig" work expanding globally and providing livelihoods to millions of low-income workers in the Global South, understanding the drivers of these workers' earnings has become increasingly important. Whereas existing research emphasizes platform design and worker characteristics as drivers of gig worker earnings, we examine another potential driver that is understudied: their social connections with more experienced workers through referral ties. We argue that such referral ties can boost gig workers' earnings through information provision by the referrer. Analyzing proprietary data from an on-demand delivery platform in India, we find that referred workers earn 14.2% more per hour than a matched sample of non-referred workers. Using difference-indifferences estimation for better econometric identification, we find that following the referrer's exit, the referred worker's hourly earnings decline by 12.5%, erasing most of the referral premium and demonstrating that the above earnings effect depends on the referrer's continued presence on the platform. Additional analyses further support an information-exchange mechanism: (i) when the referrer is concurrently online, the referred workers earn more, complete more jobs per hour, and are able to position themselves closer to high-demand areas; and (ii) upon the referrer's exit, the referred workers experience most prominent earnings declines for the more informationsensitive earnings components, where the referrer's guidance would have helped the most. Our study thus demonstrates how the mechanism of information exchange through interpersonal networks might be important even in a gig setting, at least in the Global South, where formal channels of information are often underdeveloped.

title: Yes, If: A Cognitive Task Analysis of Entrepreneurial Alertness with Serial Entrepreneurs
affiliations: Central Michigan University - College of Business Administration and Virginia Tech

detail.title: Yes, If: A Cognitive Task Analysis of Entrepreneurial Alertness with Serial Entrepreneurs
detail.abstract: Decision-making during the entrepreneurial process requires adapting to dynamic situational shifts while navigating uncertain and ill-structured environments that impact the economic success of new ventures. This study applies a cognitive task analysis approach to examine the critical decisions involved in noticing and evaluating entrepreneurial opportunities with nine serial entrepreneurs who have launched 49 startups between them. We observed seven recurring cognitive task situations within a value-creating schema: observing the status quo, assessing personal interest level, exploring the problem space, assessing the return on time and effort required, estimating the value for customers, identifying others to de-risk the opportunity, and taking action to build momentum. Participants described using heuristics as part of the procedural knowledge to determine when the composition of cues warrants further opportunity development. This set of relation structures suggests how abstract schematic mechanisms facilitate the use of adaptive expertise to reactively and proactively interact with an ill-structured and dynamic environment in order to accomplish a task.

title: The Regulated Project Participation Note: Optimal Financial Architecture under Limited Liability
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Regulated Project Participation Note: Optimal Financial Architecture under Limited Liability
detail.abstract: We introduce and analyze a project-specific, state-contingent financing instrument-the Regulated Public-Private Note (RPPN)-and compare it to standard debt in a model with endogenous effort and systemic risk. Under debt, limited liability generates payoff discontinuities that distort entrepreneurial incentives and amplify volatility through default risk. The RPPN replaces fixed repayment with proportional sharing, eliminating default thresholds and smoothing payoffs. In equilibrium, effort under debt declines with volatility, whereas effort under the RPPN is volatility-invariant. The RPPN therefore increases entrepreneurial effort, reduces asset variance, and dampens systemic risk transmission. Embedding the financing choice in a regulator's capital requirement problem, we show that optimal capital ratios are strictly lower under the RPPN. For sufficiently high volatility, the RPPN weakly dominates debt in joint equilibrium. The analysis provides a tractable framework for comparing fixed-claim and statecontingent financing under prudential regulation.

detail.abstract: Contemporary economic systems are no longer confined within single-currency environments. National currencies coexist with cross-border financial systems, institutional settlement infrastructures, digital payment networks, and emerging forms of platform-based monetary structures. As economic activity increasingly unfolds across these heterogeneous environments, the interpretation of value becomes structurally complex. Conventional monetary theory provides a coherent framework for value representation within single-currency systems. Prices denominated in a common unit allow economic agents to compare, allocate, and coordinate economic activity. However, this interpretive coherence depends on the existence of a shared monetary dimension. When economic activity extends across multiple currencies, this structural condition no longer holds. Exchange rates enable conversion between currencies, but they do not provide a unified interpretive dimension. They describe bilateral relationships rather than the structure of value across the system as a whole. Even under conditions of complete information, a multicurrency system lacks a structural framework through which value relationships can be interpreted coherently. This paper introduces the Axis Monetary System (AMS) as a structural framework that addresses this limitation. The framework is built on a fundamental separation between economic activity and value interpretation. Operational currencies, referred to as STC currencies, support transactions within their respective environments. The Axis Monetary Conversion mechanism (AMC) connects these environments, while the Axis Stability Buffer (ASB) regulates the propagation of systemic disturbances. At the center of the framework lies the value axis (AXI), an invariant structural dimension along which value relationships become interpretable. AXI is not a currency, not a financial asset, and not a unit of account. It does not participate in exchange. Instead, it provides the dimension through which relational value configurations generated by economic interaction can be interpreted as a coherent structure. Within this framework, value is not contained within currencies. Value emerges from relationships across them. Economic activity continuously reshapes these relationships, while the axis remains invariant. The system organizes these relationships through interaction, conversion, and stabilization. The contribution of this study is conceptual. It establishes the structural conditions under which value in multi-currency systems can be interpreted coherently without reducing monetary plurality to a single reference currency.

detail.abstract: Counterterrorism outside armed conflict increasingly relies on Artificial Intelligence (AI). States use AI notably for detecting, predicting, and responding to terrorism. Despite acclamations of States and regional organizations that AI needs to be used in compliance with international human rights law, there is still insufficient clarity on how human rights law guides and governs legality in the use of AI in counterterrorism. Accordingly, this chapter analyses the key human rights that are relevant to - and which help to determine the lawful use of - AI in counterterrorism. This concerns, notably, the right to privacy; the rights to liberty and security; the principle of non-discrimination; the right to freedom of expression; the right to freedom of peaceful assembly; and the rights to life and to freedom from ill-treatment. The chapter assesses how these rights concern the use of AI in counterterrorism by relating them to the functions of AI applications. This is achieved through analysis of international and national rules and jurisprudence that are directly or indirectly pertinent.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the role of demand response (DR) as a strategic flexibility resource in the long-term development and operation of power systems. Using an iterative DR module implemented in the Switch capacity expansion model, the analysis is applied to the power systems of Chile, Colombia, and Vietnam, based on models developed within the MCET network. The study assesses the contribution of DR to long-term system expansion and its implications for investment decisions in generation, storage, and transmission infrastructure through 2050. This time horizon is particularly relevant given the carbon neutrality commitments and climate targets adopted by the three countries. The results indicate that incorporating DR leads to system-wide cost reductions across all countries and scenarios, with total system costs decreasing by up to 35.7% in the Chilean case. In addition, DR consistently increases the share of renewable energy in the generation mix. By unlocking demand-side flexibility and lowering supply-side costs, DR also enables higher levels of electricity consumption, suggesting opportunities for deeper electrification and broader economic development. These findings highlight the potential of DR as a key instrument within decarbonization strategies and underscore the importance of explicitly integrating DR mechanisms into both generation and transmission planning processes.

detail.title: Hydrogen-bonded Organic Frameworks Enable in-sensor Perovskite Photoadaptation for Ultralow-power Neuromorphic Vision
detail.abstract: The emulation of biological visual systems requires exceptional adaptive capabilities that enable robust light perception across complex and dynamic conditions. However, replicating complementary photopic and scotopic adaptation in a single artificial device remains challenging due to restricted dynamic range, complex peripheral circuitry and high energy consumption. Here we pioneer a novel retinomorphic device based on a perovskite–hydrogen-bonded organic framework co-growth heterostructure (PVK@HOF), leveraging HOF to regulate PVK lattice strain. Such structural engineering empowers autonomous intensity-dependent photogenerated carrier dynamics without additional complicated circuitry, endowing PVK@HOF device with concurrent photopic and scotopic adaptation capacities. Notably, the device achieves a record low-power consumption (1.8 aJ), broad spectral responsiveness (365-800 nm), retina-equivalent response time (~180 ms), Weber-law-compliant perception, and eye-beyond high-illumination imaging ability with an ultra-wide dynamic range of 104 dB. Furthermore, a PVK@HOF visual array demonstrates over 90% object recognition accuracy in diverse autonomous driving scenarios, paving a compelling way toward next-generation vision-like imaging and in-sensor neuromorphic computing systems.

title: Emerging Trends in USA-India Foreign Trade Relations

detail.title: Emerging Trends in USA-India Foreign Trade Relations
detail.abstract: The United States and India concluded a historic Interim Trade Agreement in February 2026, marking a transformative milestone in one of the world's most strategically significant bilateral relationships. This agreement, announced on February 6, 2026, immediately reduced U.S. reciprocal tariffs on Indian goods from a peak of 50% to 18%, eliminated the punitive 25% penalty tariff imposed in 2025, and secured India's commitment to purchase USD 500 billion of American energy, technology, agricultural, and aerospace products over five years. The deal represents both a de-escalation of the 2025 trade tensions and a strategic realignment that positions the USA-India economic partnership as a central pillar of Indo-Pacific geopolitical architecture in the face of China's rising influence. This research paper provides a comprehensive examination of emerging trends in USA-India foreign trade relations through an analysis of bilateral trade statistics from 2020-2026, the negotiation dynamics and content of the February 2026 Interim Agreement, sector-by-sector impacts on key industries including pharmaceuticals, information technology, textiles, agriculture, and aerospace, the geopolitical drivers underlying the trade deal including India's Russian oil purchases and the Trump administration's reciprocal tariff doctrine, and the trajectory toward a broader Bilateral Trade Agreement (BTA) expected by late 2026 or 2027. With bilateral trade reaching USD 212.3 billion in 2024 and the United States positioned as India's largest trading partner since 2021, this paper argues that the 2026 Interim Agreement is not merely a tariff reduction exercise but a strategic economic reset that reshapes global supply chains, energy flows, and the balance of power in the Indo-Pacific region.

detail.abstract: We conduct a data-based policy evaluation of the first large-scale, EU-wide excess profit tax, implemented during the 2022 European energy crisis to tax the windfall profits of inframarginal electricity producers. In particular, we evaluate the inherent trade-off of excess profit taxation: the benefits from generating additional tax revenues for crisis mitigation versus the costs of potential distortions to production and investment decisions. On tax revenues, our analysis indicates that the inframarginal revenue cap could cover almost one quarter of the crisis-related government support, although the distribution of tax revenues and thereby the cost coverage is highly uneven across EU Member States. On distortions, we distinguish between impact on long-run investment and short-run production decisions. While we find only a limited negative impact on profitability, which could discourage investment in the long run, we find, using a difference-indifferences design, that electricity producers slightly adapt their short-run production decisions to improve their profitability. Our conclusions help to guide policymakers in future supply shocks. Excess profit taxes only provide a beneficial cost-benefit perspective under specific conditions. Policymakers must carefully time the implementation and accurately identify excess profits. Even with a generous definition of profits, excess profit taxes can be distortionary and, hence, fail to be pure windfall taxes. While retroactive implementation could be an avenue to enhance the cost-benefit profile of excess profit taxes as a crisis measure, it may undermine the credibility and predictability of the tax framework.

title: The Price of Interoperability: Exploring Cross-Chain Bridges and Their Economic Consequences
affiliations: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou),  Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou), , Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Guangzhou Campus, Society Hub and  Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)

detail.title: The Price of Interoperability: Exploring Cross-Chain Bridges and Their Economic Consequences
detail.abstract: Modern blockchain ecosystems consist of many heterogeneous networks, creating an essential need for interoperability that allows assets to move seamlessly across chains. Cross-chain bridges serve as the primary infrastructure enabling this interoperability by executing verifiable state transitions that reallocate assets and liquidity across networks. Although prior work has focused largely on bridge design and security, the system-level and economic consequences of liquidity interoperability remain poorly understood. This paper presents a large-scale empirical measurement study of cross-chain interoperability based on a comprehensive dataset covering 20 blockchains and 16 major bridge protocols from 2022 to 2025. We model the multi-chain ecosystem as a time-varying weighted hypergraph and introduce metrics to characterize blockchain interoperability via bridges. We define two metrics of interoperability. Structural interoperability captures the connectivity implied by deployed bridge infrastructure, reflecting bridge coverage and redundancy independent of user behavior. Active interoperability captures how intensively users rely on cross-chain routing in practice, measured as realized cross-chain transfer volumes normalized by chain size. This decomposition enables analysis of infrastructure capacity and utilization as distinct dimensions. Our analysis reveals several key findings. First, the cross-chain network evolves from a sparse hub-and-spoke topology into a dense, multi-hub core dominated by EVM-compatible chains. Second, we show that cross-chain capital flows are return-chasing and cost-sensitive, whereas structural interoperability primarily serves as an enabling factor rather than a directional driver of flows. Third, we identify a growth-return paradox: while higher interoperability expands ecosystem scale, it dilutes native asset value. Fourth, we uncover an efficiency-fragility trade-off: structural interoperability acts as a load balancer that reduces average gas fees, but it also synchronizes economic cycles. Bridges transform independent networks into a tightly coupled system. Finally, we show that architectural heterogeneity across bridge designs leads to distinct economic and system-level outcomes, yielding direct implications for the design of scalable and resilient cross-chain infrastructure. CCS Concepts: • Networks → Network measurement; • Applied computing → Economics.

title: Awakening the Sleeping Giant of Merger Law: The "May Tend to Create a Monopoly" Ban

detail.title: Awakening the Sleeping Giant of Merger Law: The "May Tend to Create a Monopoly" Ban
detail.abstract:
In this article we lay out a textualist analysis of Section 7’s bar against mergers that “may . . . tend to create a monopoly.” We do this using the approach to textualist statutory analysis endorsed by Justice Antonin Scalia and Bryan Garner in their influential treatment of the topic. We also analyze precedent, including old but still valid U.S. Supreme Court cases, which interpreted this second prong in ways that align with textualist originalism. 

To be clear, this is not just rigid formalism. As we explain, it would be both good law and also good economic policy to restore the “tend to create a monopoly” clause to its rightful place as a distinct, powerful, and complementary part of a vitally important statute. Using this language in Section 7 as Congress intended, antitrust enforcers and courts should examine more strictly, and prohibit where appropriate, mergers that “may . . . tend to create a monopoly.”

detail.abstract:
The German healthcare system is facing long-term structural challenges. Demographic change is leading to an increasing proportion of older people in the population, while persistently low birth rates are expected to lead to a decline in the number of economically active contributors over time. At the same time, healthcare expenditure continues to rise as a result of ongoing medical and technological progress. Concerns have also repeatedly been raised in both academic and public debates about potential incentive distortions within existing financing mechanisms, particularly the DRG-based hospital reimbursement system.
This working paper presents a reform model for financing the German healthcare system that combines pay-as-you-go and capital-funded elements. The model's core components include individual health savings accounts, a publicly organised health fund and an institutional health bank responsible for coordinating financial flows within the system. While statutory health insurance continues to provide basic coverage, health savings accounts are designed to enable the long-term accumulation of individual reserves for health-related expenditure. The health fund invests the pooled resources in a broadly diversified portfolio of national and international capital assets. The resulting investment returns contribute to the long-term stabilisation of healthcare financing.
By combining health insurance contributions, health savings accounts and a deductible component, the model establishes a multi-tier financing structure. This structure is intended to stabilise health expenditure in the long term, reduce the burden on younger contributors and increase the resilience of the healthcare system. The financial implications of the proposed model are illustrated in the appendix using exemplary calculations based on German health expenditure data.

detail.abstract: Since the second inauguration of Donald Trump, his administration has standardized draconian immigration enforcement, challenged long-standing principles of citizenship and immigration policies, and established new standards for deportation and asylum processes. Emboldened by a deferential Supreme Court, federal officials and agents are engaging in racial profiling during immigration raids, removing individuals to third countries where they have no ties, invoking the Alien Enemies Act to remove alleged gang members without hearings, accessing government data on noncitizens that were previously confidential, firing immigration judges who have high asylum approval rates, denying asylum to applicants and deporting them to apply for asylum elsewhere like Honduras under Asylum Cooperative Agreements, arresting individuals and families appearing at their removal hearings and other immigration appointments, detaining record-setting numbers, terminating Temporary Protected Status for individuals who have established roots in the United States, canceling other temporary protections previously granted to hundreds of thousands by the Biden administration, slashing refugee admissions, creating war zones in sanctuary cities viewed as sympathetic to noncitizens, expanding travel bans to nationals of dozens of countries, and halting the processing of visas for applicants from seventy-five countries. Needless to say, noncitizens and their allies—including immigration attorneys and civil rights advocates—are being challenged on a daily basis with the second Trump ICE Age. As the new Trump administration has implemented its new regime, broad counter-strategies of resistance have also emerged. From street protests to neighbors acting to protect their noncitizen friends, religious leaders chaining themselves to federal government buildings, retirees volunteering to accompany noncitizens to their hearings, impact litigators challenging policies, and non-immigration lawyers stepping up to file habeas petitions, the resistance has been steady and powerful. Patricia Williams, an early critical race theorist, has also reminded me of the role that scholars play in any resistance movement. This symposium issue of the Southwestern Law Review epitomizes that brand of resistance scholarship. While the articles themselves are excellent expressions of protest, they also serve as a foundation for contextualizing the wide and varied forms of resistance taking place that are so very important in the battle for the rights of noncitizens and the soul of the nation. In this Foreword to the symposium, I first present a brief overview of the contributions of each contributor to this volume and especially highlight policies and practices of the second Trump administration that give us reason to resist. The next Part III set forth various examples of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (“ICE”) actions that provide even more reason to resist. At the same time, those stories are good examples of truth-telling journalism that the Trump administration seeks to avoid. Part IV—the core of this essay—is a collection of some of the important examples of resistance that are taking place during this second Trump ICE Age—from attorneys and judges, to religious leaders, every day people, musicians and artists.. And Part V is closing thoughts on the importance of resistance in this arena.

detail.title: Overruling the Insular Cases: What About Federal Taxes?

publicationDetails.detailsText: NYU Journal of Law and Liberty Symposium (Forthcoming, 2026)

detail.abstract:
The Insular Cases—Supreme Court rulings from the early 1900s addressing the constitutional status of the Territories—are under fire. In 2022, Supreme Court Justice Neil Gorsuch declared “[t]hey deserve no place in our law” because they “have no foundation in the Constitution and rest instead on racial stereotypes.” Justice Sonia Sotomayor agreed, stating that the Insular Cases “were premised on beliefs both odious and wrong.” In 2024, the U.S. Justice Department established a formal policy “that the racist language and logic of the Insular Cases deserve no place in our law,” after sending a letter to Congress “condemn[ing] the racist rhetoric and reasoning of the Insular Cases” as “irreconcilable with foundational American principles of equality, justice, and democracy.” It seems only a matter of time before they are finally overruled by the U.S. Supreme Court.

While the Insular Cases have been widely condemned, legitimate questions remain over what impact overruling the Insular Cases would have on the lives of people in the Territories today. One area of particular concern many have is what revoking the Insular Cases would mean for the unique federal tax rules that currently exist in the Territories. Some go so far as to suggest that overruling the Insular Cases would trigger the immediate imposition of federal income taxes across the board in the Territories and eliminate other “favorable” tax treatment.

These concerns are misplaced. Congress has broad discretion to draw distinctions on federal taxes in the Territories largely as it sees fit—completely independent of whether the Insular Cases remain “good law.” Overruling the Insular Cases would not impact the federal tax obligations of people living in the Territories. The main reason for this is that Congress has far greater flexibility under the Constitution to establish federal tax policy than many people realize—both in the Territories and in the fifty States. Moreover, the Territories Clause of the U.S. Constitution provides an independent basis—separate and apart from the Insular Cases—for Congress to treat people in the Territories differently when it comes to questions of federal taxation and benefits.

Ultimately, the law is clear: for better or worse, Congress has broad discretion independent of the Insular Cases to regulate federal tax policy, both in the Territories and throughout the United States. Overruling the Insular Cases would not impact the federal tax obligations of those living in U.S. Territories. This reality makes it all the more certain that the Insular Cases, their racist reasoning and rhetoric, and the undemocratic colonial framework they established deserve “no place in our law” and should be overruled.

detail.abstract: We present a record-based operational template in which observable time, propagation proxies, and effective geometry arise from a typed observation pipeline under finite budgets and irreversible (many-to-one) channels. The core idea is organizational rather than microscopic: a deconfounding step removes reducible clock warps, diagonal clock conditioning selects stable snapshot records at finite resolution, and record formation is modeled as no-record evolution punctuated by exit events. This viewpoint yields a unified language for several familiar motifs: Quantummeasurement features appear as ray selection driven by record formation and by the intrinsic contraction of distinguishability under the pipeline. Relativistic clocking can be represented by hazard/exit clocks whose rate is memoryless per unit proper time in a suitable specialization, preserving a strict causal arrow in the intrinsic norecord clock. Wave-like propagation can be encoded as local two-snapshot transfer laws on the observable slice, with vacuum Maxwell as a canonical transverse update in an appropriate continuum limit. Inference artifacts such as retrograde betweensnapshot interpolation arise naturally from endpoint-conditioned reconstruction under asymmetric noise floors, without implying time travel. The framework is empirically testable as a collection of monotonicities and scaling laws: contractivity under coarse-graining, budget-limited resolution floors and plateaus, hazard/survival model selection, and protocol-class cone constraints in transport proxies. Global ontological questions are treated as partially identifiable when distinguishing signatures lie beyond record-reconstructible reach.
